{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Outsourcing Agreement (M&I)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Subject:** Playbook review findings, verified

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Outsourcing Agreement against the playbook and identified **18 findings: 14 deviations and 4 compliant items**. Two are critical.

The critical exposures are (i) **intellectual property** — Section 10.4 gives M&I outright ownership of works of authorship created for and paid for by us, with a right to resell to other customers and no licence back, reinforced by Section 17.2 ("no rights" in M&I materials) and an Article 23 source-code licence that expires with the Term; and (ii) **limitation of liability** — Section 13.4 caps only M&I's liability, at three months' payments, which sits below our six-month walk-away floor, with no carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence or willful misconduct.
",Beyond those, the Agreement is structurally weighted toward M&I on lock-in: an eight-year Term with a take-or-pay Monthly Base Fee (Article 8), sole-sourcing obligations on us (Sections 10.3(A) and 6.8), a convenience exit requiring a full year's notice plus a percentage of Estimated Remaining Value, and two Customer-payable liquidated damages amounts under Section 13.5 — one triggered by any Customer Event of Default. Governing law and venue sit in M&I's home jurisdiction (Wisconsin/Milwaukee County). Warranty, transition assistance and insurance each fail the fallback on discrete, curable points.

Four rules are **compliant and require no redline**: no non-compete binds us; there is no Vendor audit right against us; there is no MFN obligation burdening us; and the Term does not auto-renew (renewal requires mutual written agreement, with a unilateral 12-month extension option running in our favour at then-current terms).

In most instances we have targeted the **fallback** rather than the preferred position, because reaching preferred would require collateral rewrites of the payment, bundling and termination-fee machinery.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | *Redacted* (edits at 10.4/10.5, 17.2, 17.4) | Add numbered Section 10.5 granting a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Developed Software; conform 17.2; limit M&I's use of Customer Data in 17.4 to providing the Services. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 13 Damages | Make the Section 13.4 cap mutual and based on 12 months' fees; add carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 10 Modification or Termination of Services | Remove our obligations to source all Monthly Base Fee Services (10.3(A)) and Bankcard Services processing (6.8) from M&I; M&I becomes non-exclusive. |
| 4 | High | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 14 Insurance and Indemnity | Add infringement remedies (procure/modify/replace, else refund) and a 3x annual fees super-cap on 14.2(B), carved out of the Section 13.4 cap. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 13 Damages | Cap the Termination for Convenience Fee at three months' fees; remove the Termination for Cause Fee (conforming 11.2(A)); make the early-termination fee the sole liquidated amount payable by us. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 11 Termination | Cut our convenience notice to 90 days and cap all Section 11.1 early-termination amounts at three months' fees; limit M&I's Section 10.2 withdrawal of non-Core Services to the end of the Term. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Compliant** | § 21.4 (and Articles 3, 10, 17, 21–23 checked) | Preferred position met; no covenant restricts our businesses, providers or products. Sections 21.7(B) and 23.5 are licence-scope terms only. No redline. |
| 8 | Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 22 Miscellaneous (22.4) | Mutual successor assignment on written notice; broaden our carve-out to "assets, stock or securities"; remove "freely"; delete M&I's consent-free divisional-transfer exception at (b)(ii). |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Compliant** | § 21.4 (also 21.8, 21.9(B)–(C), 17.1, 22.12) | All audit/examination rights run in our favour or to our regulators. No redline — adding an audit-limitation clause would invite a right that does not exist. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 22 Miscellaneous (22.1–22.2) | Move governing law to New York and exclusive merits venue to New York County courts; judgment-enforcement consent preserved. |
| 11 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 23 Source Code | Make the source-code licence transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition of Customer; conform the Section 23.5(1) transfer prohibition. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | **Compliant** | § 8 Fees | No MFN, best-terms or right-to-match obligation runs in M&I's favour. Preferred position met; no redline. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Deviation | § 8 Fees | New Section 8.1A capping the Monthly Base Fee commitment at the then-current 12-month period, with reduction on 30 days' notice and true-up of any shortfall without penalty; 10.3.A made subject to that reduction right. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 22 Miscellaneous (22.14) | Narrow the mutual non-solicit to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months post-involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. Remains solicitation-only. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Compliant** | § 2 Term (2.2) | No automatic renewal; renewal requires mutual written agreement. Our extension option is at then-current terms. Preferred position; no redline. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | Deviation | *Redacted* (edits at 11.4; 17.1/17.5 context) | Add a guaranteed minimum 90-day Termination Assistance period following any expiry or termination and export of all Customer Data within 30 days; existing then-current-rate and six-month mechanics untouched. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 16.1 (By M&I) | Add subsection G: 90-day software-to-documentation conformance warranty with repair, replacement or refund remedy (automatically carved out of the 16.1.F disclaimer). |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 14 Insurance and Indemnity (14.1(A)) | Add professional liability (E&O) of USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy of USD 2,000,000; existing certificate and cancellation-notice mechanic already extends to the new coverage. |

*Note: two findings reference sections recorded as redacted in the copy reviewed; the edits are placed against the operative provisions identified in the rationale.*

---

## Walk-away items

These are the terms we cannot accept as drafted:

1. **Liability cap below the floor (Section 13.4).** The cap is one-sided and set at three months' payments, below our six-month walk-away floor, and by its terms overrides every other provision — so the Vendor IP indemnity sits inside it. We require a mutual 12-month fees cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct, plus a 3x annual fees super-cap on the indemnity.
2. **Sole-sourcing obligations (Sections 10.3(A) and 6.8).** Full-Term commitments to take all Monthly Base Fee Services, and to use M&I primarily for Bankcard Services processing, with no category-and-12-month limit and no automatic exit for service level or delivery failures. This sits in walk-away territory; M&I must be non-exclusive.
3. **Termination for Cause Fee (Sections 11.2(A) and 13.5).** A liquidated amount measured by the full remaining Term and triggered by any Customer Event of Default — or merely by failing to give the Section 11.1 notice. Penalising a minor breach on a remaining-term measure is walk-away territory; the fee must be removed.
4. **Ownership of paid-for work product (Section 10.4, with 17.2 and Article 23).** M&I owning, and being free to resell, work we commissioned and paid for, with no licence back and only Term-limited use rights, is not acceptable. At minimum we need the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence in the proposed Section 10.5.

We also flag the **non-solicit (Section 22.14)** as approaching walk-away: it covers all employees of the other party for the entire multi-year Term with no advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the 14 deviations, marked with the `[Playbook]` comment prefix and, where we have moved to the fallback rather than the preferred position, a one-line note explaining the trade-off.
2. **Sequence the negotiation.** Open on the four walk-away items (liability cap and indemnity super-cap; exclusivity; Termination for Cause Fee; IP licence-back). Treat governing law, source-code transferability, warranty, transition and insurance as a second package likely to close with limited resistance.
3. **Confirm the redacted provisions.** Obtain unredacted text for the Section 10.4/17.x IP provisions, the Section 11.1 fee percentage and Section 11.3 before finalising, and re-verify the IP and transition edits against it.
4. **Coordinate internally.** Sponsor input on the Monthly Base Fee reduction mechanic (Section 8.1A) and on alternative bankcard/data-processing providers, given the eight-year Term; risk and treasury sign-off on the E&O and cyber limits.
5. **Record the compliant items** (non-compete, audit, MFN, renewal) in the file as reviewed and deliberately not redlined, so they are not reopened on later turns."}
